rows.opening: docker pull fails with 'You have reached your pull rate limit' HTTP 429 from Docker Hub

fixes_sent.message:
You have exceeded the Docker Hub pull rate limit for unauthenticated or Docker Personal users based on your IP address or account tier.

1. Authenticate or upgrade your Docker account to increase your rate limit. [E1]
2. Wait until your pull rate limit decreases, and then try again. [E1]

To confirm: Check your current pull rate and limit headers using curl and jq, or successfully pull images without receiving the HTTP 429 error.

Sources: E1 https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/main/content/manuals/docker-hub/troubleshoot.md

Did this resolve the issue?
sources: You have reached your pull rate limit (429 response code)

evidence.text:
When this issue occurs, you receive following error message in the Docker CLI or
in the Docker Engine logs:

```text
You have reached your pull rate limit. You may increase the limit by authenticating and upgrading: https://www.docker.com/increase-rate-limits
```

- You have reached your pull rate limit as an authenticated Docker Personal
  user.
- You have reached your pull rate limit as an unauthenticated user based on your
  IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet.

You can use one of the following solutions:

- [Authenticate](./usage/pulls.md#authentication) or
  [upgrade](../subscription-billing/manage/plans.md#upgrade-plans) your Docker
  account.
- [View your pull rate limit](./usage/pulls.md#view-hourly-pull-rate-and-limit),
  wait until your pull rate limit decreases, and then try again.

rows.opening: Docker Hub pulls are failing with a 429 error

fixes_sent.message:
You have reached the Docker Hub abuse rate limit, which returns a 429 Too Many Requests response when thousands of requests per minute are sent.

1. Check for broken CI/CD pipelines accessing Docker Hub and fix them. [E1]
2. Implement a retry with back-off solution in your automated scripts to ensure that you're not resending thousands of requests per minute. [E1]

To confirm: Confirm that your automated scripts and CI/CD pipelines no longer flood Docker Hub with excessive requests and successfully pull images without receiving the 429 error.

Sources: E1 https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/main/content/manuals/docker-hub/troubleshoot.md

Did this resolve the issue?
